title: Agent approvals & security – Codex
relevance_note: Official control-surface doc for approval prompts, protected paths, and destructive app-tool gating.
reason_included: Contains concrete approval classes and boundary conditions that directly affect harness gate design.

claim_snippets.claim_text: In workspace-write mode, protected paths inside writable roots remain read-only, including .git, .agents, and .codex, and protection is recursive.
Granular approval policy can keep some prompt categories interactive while automatically rejecting others, including request_permissions and skill-script approvals.
Destructive app or MCP tool calls always require approval when the tool advertises a destructive annotation, even if the tool also advertises other hints such as read-only hints.

In the Auto preset, Codex can read files, make edits, and run commands in the working directory automatically, but it still asks for approval to edit outside the workspace or to run commands that require network access.
